    Power calculations for co-primary diagnostic accuracy endpoints - Comparative designs

    power.copr.comp.test.Rd

    Computes either the required total sample size or the achieved overall power of a comparative confirmatory diagnostic accuracy study with co-primary endpoints (sensitivity and specificity). Exactly one of N and power must be NULL. The one that is NULL is calculated.

    Two designs are available:

    • design = "unpaired": subjects are randomised to the experimental or the comparator test. The endpoints compare two independent proportions.

    • design = "paired": all subjects receive both tests. The discordance probabilities psi.d (diseased) and psi.nd (non-diseased) can be specified, or alternatively the correlations rho.d and rho.nd (one of the two per endpoint). Without either, the lower Stark bound is used.

    Superiority and non-inferiority hypotheses may be specified independently for sensitivity and specificity. The study is successful only if both endpoint null hypotheses are rejected (intersection-union test, IUT), so the type I error rate is controlled at level alpha without multiplicity adjustment.

    power.copr.comp.test(
  N = NULL,
  power = NULL,
  prev,
  design = c("unpaired", "paired"),
  se.c,
  se.e,
  sp.c,
  sp.e,
  alpha = 0.025,
  psi.d = NULL,
  psi.nd = NULL,
  rho.d = NULL,
  rho.nd = NULL,
  delta.se = 0,
  delta.sp = 0,
  type.se = c("sup", "ni"),
  type.sp = c("sup", "ni"),
  variance = c("null", "pooled", "unpooled"),
  alternative = c("one.sided", "two.sided"),
  exact = FALSE,
  exact_rule = c("first", "stays_above")
)

    Arguments

    N

    Sample size, or NULL to calculate it. Participants per arm (unpaired) or in total (paired).

    power

    Desired overall power, or NULL to calculate it.

    prev

    Disease prevalence (0 < prev < 1).

    design

    "unpaired" (default) or "paired".

    se.c

    Sensitivity of the comparator test.

    se.e

    Sensitivity of the experimental test.

    sp.c

    Specificity of the comparator test.

    sp.e

    Specificity of the experimental test.

    alpha

    Type I error level per endpoint (default 0.025). It is the one-sided level unless alternative = "two.sided", in which case the critical value uses alpha / 2.

    psi.d

    Discordance probability in the diseased (only for design = "paired"). At most one of psi.d and rho.d may be given. If neither is, the lower bound of Stark et al. (2022), abs(se.c - se.e), is used and a message is printed. This is the smallest possible discordance and gives the smallest sample size.

    psi.nd

    Discordance probability in the non-diseased. As psi.d, with default abs(sp.c - sp.e).

    rho.d

    Correlation of the two tests' results in the diseased, as an alternative to psi.d (only for design = "paired").

    rho.nd

    Correlation of the two tests' results in the non-diseased, as an alternative to psi.nd (only for design = "paired").

    delta.se

    Non-inferiority margin for sensitivity (used only if type.se = "ni").

    delta.sp

    Non-inferiority margin for specificity (used only if type.sp = "ni").

    type.se

    Type of hypothesis for sensitivity: "sup" (superiority, default) or "ni" (non-inferiority).

    type.sp

    Type of hypothesis for specificity: "sup" (superiority, default) or "ni" (non-inferiority).

    variance

    Only for design = "unpaired": variance of the difference estimator under the null used for the critical value: "null" (default, variance at the comparator proportion for superiority, alternative variance for non-inferiority), "pooled" (pooled proportion \((c+e)/2\)) or "unpooled" (alternative variance). The alternative variance is always unpooled.

    alternative

    "one.sided" (default) or "two.sided".

    exact

    Experimental. Only for design = "unpaired": use the exact binomial power of the Wald test (estimated variance, variance = "unpooled" by default or "pooled") instead of the normal approximation. N must then be an integer, split into round(N * prev) diseased and the remaining non-diseased subjects per arm. See Details. Default FALSE.

    exact_rule

    Only for exact = TRUE and a given power: "first" (default, smallest \(N\) reaching the target) or "stays_above" (smallest \(N\) from which the power stays at or above the target).

    Value

    An object of class "power.htest", a list with the elements:

    n

    Sample size N: per arm for the unpaired design, total number of participants for the paired design.

    n_dis

    Number of diseased subjects (per arm for the unpaired design).

    n_nondis

    Number of non-diseased subjects (per arm for the unpaired design).

    prev

    Disease prevalence.

    sig.level

    Type I error level.

    alternative

    "one.sided" or "two.sided".

    power

    Overall power.

    power_se

    Power for the sensitivity endpoint.

    power_sp

    Power for the specificity endpoint.

    type.se

    Hypothesis type for sensitivity.

    type.sp

    Hypothesis type for specificity.

    psi.d, psi.nd

    Discordance used (paired design only). It is converted from rho.d / rho.nd if those were given.

    variance

    Variance used (unpaired design only).

    exact

    Whether exact binomial power was used (unpaired design only).

    target_power

    Requested power (only when power was given).

    exact_rule

    Rule used (only for exact = TRUE and a given power).

    Details

    Let \(\pi\) denote the prevalence. Sensitivity is evaluated in the \(N\pi\) diseased and specificity in the \(N(1-\pi)\) non-diseased subjects (per arm in the unpaired design, where \(N\) is the size of each arm). These subgroups are independent, so $$\mathrm{Power}_{\mathrm{Overall}} = \mathrm{Power}_{\mathrm{Se}} \times \mathrm{Power}_{\mathrm{Sp}}.$$

    Unpaired design. Large-sample normal approximation for the difference of two independent proportions with variance \(\theta_C(1-\theta_C) + \theta_E(1-\theta_E)\) per subject, where \(\theta_C\) and \(\theta_E\) are the comparator and experimental sensitivity (or specificity), i.e. se.c, se.e (or sp.c, sp.e). For superiority the critical value uses the null variance chosen by variance. For non-inferiority the alternative variance is used with the margin delta. The sample size is the smallest integer \(N\) whose overall power reaches the target.

    Paired design. Superiority uses the asymptotic formula of Stark et al. (2022, Miettinen). Non-inferiority uses the restricted maximum likelihood (score) test of Liu et al. (2002), with the variance of the estimated difference evaluated at the boundary of the null hypothesis. Both depend on the discordance \(\psi\), which must lie in the interval of Stark et al. (2022, Eq. 10), \(|d| \le \psi \le c + e - 2ce\), where \(c\) and \(e\) are the comparator and experimental sensitivity (or specificity) and \(d = e - c\) their difference. This corresponds to non-negative correlation between the two tests. Negative correlation is not considered. The sample size increases with \(\psi\). If no discordance is specified, its lower bound \(|d|\) is used, as in the worked example of Stark et al. As for the unpaired design, the sample size is the smallest integer \(N\) whose overall power reaches the target.

    The dependence between the tests may be given as a correlation (rho.d, rho.nd, phi coefficient of the two binary results) instead of the discordance. The correlation is converted once, at the alternative, to the discordance with rho_to_psi. All calculations, including the null quantities of the Liu et al. (2002) score test, then use this discordance exactly as if psi.d / psi.nd had been given. The correlation must lie between 0 and its maximum for the given sensitivities (or specificities). Use paired_bounds to see the feasible ranges before the calculation.

    Exact power (unpaired design, experimental). This option is still experimental: it needs further development and testing, and its interface and results may change. With exact = TRUE the power is the exact probability, over two independent binomial counts per endpoint, that the Wald statistic with estimated variance exceeds the critical value (the same test as in power.copr.comp.emp). The "null" variance has no exact counterpart, so "unpooled" is used unless variance = "pooled" is given. The exact power is not monotone in \(N\), so the sample size is found by a scan around the asymptotic solution (see exact_rule and power.copr.test). The sums neglect binomial tail probabilities below \(10^{-12}\).

    References

    Stark, M., Hesse, M., Brannath, W., & Zapf, A. (2022). Blinded sample size re-estimation in a comparative diagnostic accuracy study. BMC Medical Research Methodology, 22, 115. doi:10.1186/s12874-022-01564-2

    Liu, J., Hsueh, H., Hsieh, E., & Chen, J. J. (2002). Tests for equivalence or non-inferiority for paired binary data. Statistics in Medicine, 21(2), 231-245. doi:10.1002/sim.1012

    See also

    power.copr.test for the single-test design, paired_bounds and rho_to_psi for the paired dependence parameters.

    Author

    Maia Muresan & Ainesh Sewak (DCR Bern)

    Examples

    # Unpaired design: sample size, then power at that sample size
power.copr.comp.test(power = 0.80, prev = 0.6,
                     se.c = 0.75, se.e = 0.85,
                     sp.c = 0.65, sp.e = 0.75)
#> 
#>      Comparative unpaired design (sample size calculation)
#>                    Wald normal approximation 
#> 
#>               n = 909
#>           n_dis = 545.4
#>        n_nondis = 363.6
#>            prev = 0.6
#>       sig.level = 0.025
#>     alternative = one.sided
#>           power = 0.8003529
#>        power_se = 0.9784401
#>        power_sp = 0.8179886
#>    target_power = 0.8
#>         type.se = sup
#>         type.sp = sup
#>        variance = null
#>           exact = FALSE
#> 
#> NOTE: n is the total sample size.
#> 
power.copr.comp.test(N = 910, prev = 0.6,
                     se.c = 0.75, se.e = 0.85,
                     sp.c = 0.65, sp.e = 0.75)
#> 
#>      Comparative unpaired design (power calculation)
#>                 Wald normal approximation 
#> 
#>               n = 910
#>           n_dis = 546
#>        n_nondis = 364
#>            prev = 0.6
#>       sig.level = 0.025
#>     alternative = one.sided
#>           power = 0.8008698
#>        power_se = 0.9785579
#>        power_sp = 0.8184184
#>         type.se = sup
#>         type.sp = sup
#>        variance = null
#>           exact = FALSE
#> 
#> NOTE: n is the total sample size.
#> 

# Unpaired, exact binomial power at an integer N
power.copr.comp.test(N = 300, prev = 0.6, exact = TRUE,
                     se.c = 0.75, se.e = 0.85,
                     sp.c = 0.65, sp.e = 0.75)
#> 
#>      Comparative unpaired design (power calculation)
#>       Exact binomial (Wald test, unpooled variance) 
#> 
#>               n = 300
#>           n_dis = 180
#>        n_nondis = 120
#>            prev = 0.6
#>       sig.level = 0.025
#>     alternative = one.sided
#>           power = 0.2677276
#>        power_se = 0.6680888
#>        power_sp = 0.4007366
#>         type.se = sup
#>         type.sp = sup
#>        variance = unpooled
#>           exact = TRUE
#> 
#> NOTE: n is the total sample size.
#> 

# Unpaired, specificity non-inferiority
power.copr.comp.test(power = 0.80, prev = 0.6,
                     se.c = 0.75, se.e = 0.85,
                     sp.c = 0.65, sp.e = 0.75,
                     delta.sp = 0.05, type.sp = "ni")
#> 
#>      Comparative unpaired design (sample size calculation)
#>                    Wald normal approximation 
#> 
#>               n = 545
#>           n_dis = 327
#>        n_nondis = 218
#>            prev = 0.6
#>       sig.level = 0.025
#>     alternative = one.sided
#>           power = 0.800697
#>        power_se = 0.8606962
#>        power_sp = 0.9302899
#>    target_power = 0.8
#>         type.se = sup
#>         type.sp = ni
#>        variance = null
#>           exact = FALSE
#> 
#> NOTE: n is the total sample size.
#> 

# Paired design with discordances (default if omitted: lower Stark bound)
power.copr.comp.test(power = 0.80, prev = 0.47, design = "paired",
                     se.c = 0.81, se.e = 0.90,
                     sp.c = 0.66, sp.e = 0.80,
                     psi.d = 0.09, psi.nd = 0.14)
#> 
#>      Comparative paired design (sample size calculation)
#>            Score normal approximation (Miettinen) 
#> 
#>               n = 133
#>           n_dis = 62.51
#>        n_nondis = 70.49
#>            prev = 0.47
#>       sig.level = 0.025
#>     alternative = one.sided
#>           power = 0.8017429
#>        power_se = 0.8061094
#>        power_sp = 0.9945832
#>    target_power = 0.8
#>         type.se = sup
#>         type.sp = sup
#>           psi.d = 0.09
#>          psi.nd = 0.14
#> 
#> NOTE: n is the total sample size.
#> 
power.copr.comp.test(N = 134, prev = 0.47, design = "paired",
                     se.c = 0.81, se.e = 0.90,
                     sp.c = 0.66, sp.e = 0.80,
                     psi.d = 0.09, psi.nd = 0.14,
                     delta.sp = 0.05, type.sp = "ni")
#> 
#>        Comparative paired design (power calculation)
#>      Score normal approximation (Miettinen / Liu score) 
#> 
#>               n = 134
#>           n_dis = 62.98
#>        n_nondis = 71.02
#>            prev = 0.47
#>       sig.level = 0.025
#>     alternative = one.sided
#>           power = 0.8003348
#>        power_se = 0.8111949
#>        power_sp = 0.9866122
#>         type.se = sup
#>         type.sp = ni
#>           psi.d = 0.09
#>          psi.nd = 0.14
#> 
#> NOTE: n is the total sample size.
#> 

# Paired design with correlations instead of discordances
paired_bounds(se.c = 0.81, se.e = 0.90, sp.c = 0.66, sp.e = 0.80)
#>      endpoint psi.min psi.max rho.min   rho.max
#> 1 sensitivity    0.09   0.252       0 0.6882472
#> 2 specificity    0.14   0.404       0 0.6966305
power.copr.comp.test(power = 0.80, prev = 0.47, design = "paired",
                     se.c = 0.81, se.e = 0.90,
                     sp.c = 0.66, sp.e = 0.80,
                     rho.d = 0.5, rho.nd = 0.3)
#> 
#>      Comparative paired design (sample size calculation)
#>            Score normal approximation (Miettinen) 
#> 
#>               n = 290
#>           n_dis = 136.3
#>        n_nondis = 153.7
#>            prev = 0.47
#>       sig.level = 0.025
#>     alternative = one.sided
#>           power = 0.8001468
#>        power_se = 0.8700683

#> 
#> NOTE: n is the total sample size.
#>
